To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a DEAD box protein, DDX3 is involved in cell cycle progression and apoptosis, and is deregulated in HBV- but not HCV-associated HCC.

the deregulation (downregulation) of a DEAD box RNA (ribonucleic acid) helicase, a protein that regulates cell growth, is associated with hepatocellular carcinoma (liver cancer) in hepatitis B virus-positive patients.

the deregulation pattern of a DEAD box RNA-helicase DDX3, which is involved in cell cycle regulation, is correlated with hepatitis virus-associated hepatoblastoma development and progression, and this deregulation may contribute to hepatocarcinogenic processes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the involvement of Ddx3 in hepatocellular carcinoma (hcc), a common cancer of the liver.
the role of DDX family members in the development of HCV-related HCV.
the role of DDX 3, a DEAD-box RNA helicase that is targeted by HCV core protein, in hepatocarcininogenesis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
DDX3 is involved in the pathogenesis of HBV- but not HCV-associated HCC.
the downregualtion of DDX3 may contribute to the development of HCCs from HBV-infected patients and that DDX3 may function as a tumor suppressor in hepatocarcinoses.
DDX3 is down-regulated in HBV-associated HCC, but not in HCV-associated HCC, and that this downregulation is associated with cell growth promotion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the deregulation and the functions of DDX3 are involved in hepatitis virus-associated carcinogenesis.
DDX3 is involved in cell transformation and hepatocarcinogeneses, and that its deregulation in HCC is correlated with hepatitis virus infections.
DDX3, as a novel cell growth regulator, is involved in the pathogenesis of hepatitis virus-associated hepatobiliary cancers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the deregulation or dysregulation of Ddx3 expression is associated with the development of HCC.
DDX3 is involved in cell cycle regulation.
DDX3 expression was significantly down-regulated in HCCs compared to the corresponding non-tumor tissues from HBV-positive patients, but not in HCV-positive ones.
